sentences.text:
Vs. Govt. of NCT, Delhi along with Civil Appeal No. 6637 of 2010 reported in 2019 (4) PLJR (SC) 383, in which it has been decided that in the matter of acquisition under National Highways Act, 1956,
there is no applicability of Section 33 of the Act of RFCTLARRA, 2013 (Act No.30 of 2013).

13. In view of this Court, section 33 of RFCTLARRA, 2013 (Act No.30 of 2013) shall not be applicable in the present case at Patna High Court CWJC No.11006 of 2019(7)
dt.08-04-2024 all as the preparation of second award amounts to review of the earlier award and under law, the competent Authority being quasi judicial authority has no power to review its own order and without any authority under law the applicability of Section 33 of the RFCTLARRA, 2013 (Act No.30 of 2013) is for very limited purpose which itself laid down in the Statute.
14.
In this background, this Court is of the view that preparation of later award if absolutely bad in law in all the cases.

As such, award dated 30.07.2018 in CWJC No.
5750 of 2019, CWJC No. 5908 of 2019, CWJC No. 5930 of 2019, CWJC No. 7402 of 2019, CWJC No. 7438 of 2019, CWJC No. 7715 of 2019 and award dated 02.07.2018 in CWJC No. 7437 of 2019 are hereby set- aside.

15. Accordingly, this writ petition is allowed granting liberty to the NHAI that if it has grievances from the earlier award then the Patna High Court CWJC No.11006 of 2019(7) dt.08-04-2024 NHAI may take recourse to Section 3G (5) of the Act of 1956 by way of filing appropriate application before the Arbitrator -cum- Divisional Commissioner concerned.
16. With the aforesaid directions and observations, the writ petitions stand disposed off.
3. On specific query, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the NHAI submits that the said order has not been challenged.
4. Accordingly, this Court also takes the route of C.W.J.C. No. 5750 of 2019.
